correctness.rationale: Exact block-contraction calculations yield the one-pair mean and second binomial moment. Conditional relabelling makes pair events pairwise independent even when they share one order index; disjoint-index variables admit an exact dependency graph. The classical local-dependency Poisson theorem bounds total variation by O(r^3 p^2) and replacing indicator events by full runs costs O(r^2 beta). Monotonicity plus subsampling, one-edge second moments, Markov bounds, and equivariant witness choice prove all extreme-value and isolation assertions. Exact finite checks reproduce all contraction identities through n=8; they are corroboration, not asymptotic proof.
